Early mobilisation and 90-day mortality in adults receiving mechanical ventilation
Smith J, Okafor A, Lindqvist P, et al. N Engl J Med. 2024. PMID 38123456 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38123456/). DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2400001 (https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2400001).

CLINICAL QUESTION (PICO)
  Population:   Adults in intensive care ventilated for at least 48 hours
  Intervention: Structured early mobilisation started within 72 hours of intubation
  Comparison:   Usual physiotherapy at the discretion of the treating team
  Outcome:      Death from any cause within 90 days

STUDY DESIGN
  Randomized controlled trial (parallel)
  Detected from publication type. Evidence: Randomized Controlled Trial (publication type), randomly assigned (abstract keyword).

KEY RESULTS
  CER (control event rate):      26.0%
  EER (experimental event rate): 16.0%
  ARR (absolute risk reduction): 10.0 percentage points (95% CI 3.5 to 16.5)
  RRR (relative risk reduction): 38.5%
  NNT 10 (95% CI 7–29)

VALIDITY
  1. Can you tell how participants were assigned to the groups, and does the method described rely on chance rather than on a predictable order?
     Verdict: Yes
  2. Does the abstract tell you whether the people enrolling each participant could have known which group that person was about to get?
     Verdict: Unclear
  3. Do you know who was kept unaware of the assigned group: the participants, the treating clinicians, the outcome assessors, or none of them?
     Verdict: No
  4. Does the abstract show that the groups started out alike in the characteristics that drive the outcome, such as age, severity and prior treatment?
     Verdict: Yes
  5. Can you see how many participants were followed to the end, and whether the losses were similar in size and in reason across the groups?
     Verdict: Yes
  6. Does the abstract say whether participants were analysed in the group they were assigned to, even if they stopped, switched or never started that treatment?
     Verdict: —
  7. Is one primary outcome named and defined precisely enough that you could check it against the registered protocol?
     Verdict: Yes
  8. Do you know who funded the trial and what part the sponsor played in its design, analysis and reporting?
     Verdict: No
  9. Are the participants, the dose and the comparison close enough to the patients and the usual care you know for the result to carry over?
     Verdict: —
  Notes on items answered No or Unclear:
    Item 2 (Unclear): The abstract says "randomly assigned" and nothing about who held the sequence.
    Item 3 (No): Open label. Mortality is a hard endpoint, so this matters less here than it would for a symptom score.
    Item 8 (No): (no note)

BOTTOM LINE
  A 10 percentage point difference in 90-day mortality is large for this population, and the trial was stopped early at an interim look, so the estimate is probably optimistic. I would read the methods before taking the size of the effect at face value.
